Analyst.contrast_definition: From t=0 with matched saved random priors, random streams, checkpoint and native protocol; one registered intervention versus its parent. Chemical graphs remain free; historical suffix score levels are not from-zero treatment effects.
Analyst.falsifier: The hypothesis is falsified if, under the banded operator on the same N22 support and dose, the from-zero paired terminal affinity distribution is not distinguishable from the parent pointwise run (no measurable change in mean_all_pic50, best_qualified_pic50, U_tau or hit_fraction beyond the paired uncertainty), or if formation/retention collapses (near-zero active updates, large assignment switching, or clipping) so that the banded observable is not actually formed and retained. It is also falsified if the banded run's measured formation/retention statistics match the parent but the terminal affinity is worse in a way attributable to the band rather than to noise.
Analyst.observable_definition: Implemented and derivative-tested: squared excess of local point distance outside a calibrated spatial tolerance. A coordinate intervention to be tested, not a proven affinity rule.
Analyst.predicted_execution_response: Under the banded operator on the same N22 support, expect active/nonzero updates comparable to the parent (near 40), no atom clipping, injected RMS near the parent's ~0.0298 A, and point_rms_A / target_error that are bounded by the band rather than driven to the parent's ~0.0757 A mean. Assignment switch fraction should remain small. If the band is too wide, the observable becomes nearly flat and updates shrink; if too narrow, excess is large and the run behaves closer to the parent pointwise curvature.
Analyst.predicted_terminal_response: Terminal affinity is not forecast from the source layout score. The measured comparison is the from-zero paired terminal distribution of the banded run versus the parent pointwise run on the same prior, RNG, checkpoint and native protocol. A plausible outcome is a terminal mean_all_pic50 and best_qualified_pic50 in the neighborhood of the parent's 7.5364 / 8.1268, with U_tau and hit_fraction reported as measured; any improvement or degradation must be read from the paired from-zero comparison, not from historical suffix levels.
Analyst.scientific_hypothesis: Within the N22 local support, the parent pointwise robust per-point distance to observed teacher coordinates is not the only geometric observable that can be formed and retained. Replacing it with a banded local point-distance observable (point_band) on the same six-slot support, same pocket_sites, same bridge representation and same dose should still form and retain a local geometric match to the teacher coordinates, but with a different terminal affinity profile than the parent pointwise run. The two competing explanations are: (i) the parent pointwise curvature is the operative geometric channel and any banded variant will degrade terminal affinity; (ii) the parent pointwise curvature is not uniquely required, and a banded tolerance around the same local target coordinates can preserve formation/retention while changing terminal affinity. The discriminating observable is the paired from-zero terminal affinity distribution and the measured formation/retention statistics under the banded operator versus the parent pointwise run.

Designer.falsifier: Execution-level: the banded observable is not actually formed and retained if the run shows near-zero active/nonzero updates, large assignment switching, or clipping, or if measured point_rms_A/target_error are not bounded by the band. Terminal: the hypothesis is falsified if the from-zero paired terminal affinity distribution of the banded run is not distinguishable from parent R13_v2 (no measurable change in mean_all_pic50, best_qualified_pic50, U_tau or hit_fraction beyond paired uncertainty), or if formation/retention matches the parent but terminal affinity is worse in a way attributable to the band rather than to noise. Affinity is evaluated first; structural and energy side effects are reported using the frozen definitions.
Designer.operator_definition: Implemented and derivative-tested: squared excess of local point distance outside a calibrated spatial tolerance. A coordinate intervention to be tested, not a proven affinity rule.

Designer.predicted_control_response: Under point_band on the same N22 support and dose, expect active/nonzero updates comparable to the parent's 40, no atom clipping, injected RMS near the parent's ~0.0298 A mean, and point_rms_A / target_error bounded by the band rather than driven to the parent's ~0.0757 A mean. Assignment switch fraction should remain small (parent mean ~1.8e-4). If the band is too wide the observable flattens and updates shrink; if too narrow the run behaves closer to the parent pointwise curvature. These are expectations to be measured, not established outcomes.
Designer.scientific_rationale: Single-factor from-zero contrast on the same N22 six-slot support, same pocket_sites, same bridge representation, same dose, same saved prior/RNG/checkpoint/native protocol as parent R13_v2; only the operator changes pointwise -> point_band. The parent pointwise observable is a robust per-point distance to observed teacher coordinates; point_band replaces it with squared excess outside a calibrated tolerance band, so the two hypotheses (parent curvature uniquely required vs. banded tolerance sufficient for formation/retention) are discriminated by the paired from-zero terminal affinity distribution plus measured formation/retention statistics. The band basis (quarter source local covalent-length median, base_band_A 0.3478160934503709) is a proposed calibration, not a proven success tolerance; band_multiplier stays at the parent value 1.0 so the band is not co-varied with the operator change. Historical suffix levels and source layout score are not from-zero treatment effects and are not used to forecast terminal affinity.
